title: Feature Flag & Progressive Rollout Platform with MurmurHash3 Bucketing
problem: Software engineering teams must decouple code deployment from feature release to minimize production blast radiuses and perform gradual canary validations. Deploying features directly to all users simultaneously risks widespread service degradation, while coordinating rollouts via manual code releases slows engineering velocity. This project builds a high-performance feature flag and progressive rollout platform in Go, React, PostgreSQL, and Redis. The system supports percentage rollouts using deterministic MurmurHash3 user bucketing, complex attribute targeting rules (e.g., country, subscription tier, beta tag), sub-millisecond local in-memory flag evaluation, Server-Sent Events (SSE) for real-time flag push propagation without polling, and an administrative React dashboard with real-time audit logs and instant kill-switches.
use_cases: Continuous delivery pipelines executing progressive percentage canary rollouts (1% to 10% to 100%)
Targeted beta feature releases restricted to specific customer subscription tiers and internal employee emails
Emergency kill-switch activation instantly disabling broken third-party integrations across clusters without redeployment
hard_parts: Implementing deterministic MurmurHash3 user bucketing so a user remains consistently assigned to the same variant
Propagating flag configuration updates in real-time across distributed client instances via Server-Sent Events (SSE)
Achieving sub-millisecond evaluation latency in local SDK memory while guaranteeing dynamic rule synchronization
Building an atomic administrative audit trail in PostgreSQL that records every rule change, variant shift, and kill-switch toggle
screener_signals: Clean full-stack implementation separating Go evaluation engine, SSE streamer, React admin dashboard, and Redis pub/sub
Deterministic uniform distribution benchmark proving MurmurHash3 distributes 100,000 users evenly within 1.5% variance
Anti-fake verification script toggling an emergency kill-switch and asserting that client evaluation flips instantly within 50ms

components.name: MurmurHash3 User Bucketing Engine
components.purpose: Calculates deterministic 32-bit hash integers for user keys to ensure consistent percentage rollout assignment

components.name: Targeting Rule Evaluation Engine
components.purpose: Evaluates user attributes (country, tier, email regex) against declarative boolean rule criteria

components.name: SSE Real-Time Push Streamer
components.purpose: Pushes instantaneous flag configuration diffs to connected client SDKs via Server-Sent Events

components.name: React Administration Dashboard
components.purpose: Provides user interface for creating flags, configuring rollout percentages, and toggling emergency kill-switches

architecture.data_flow: Administrators create or modify flags in the React Dashboard; the Go API validates changes, appends an entry to PostgreSQL audit logs, and commits updated rules; the server publishes an invalidation event to Redis Pub/Sub; the SSE Push Streamer broadcasts the new configuration to connected client applications over persistent HTTP streams; client SDKs update their local in-memory flag caches; incoming evaluation requests compute MurmurHash3 hashes across user ID and flag key to determine variant assignment locally in sub-millisecond time.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Deterministic hashing preventing user bucket flapping; atomic PostgreSQL transactions recording audit records before publishing updates.

targets.method: Microbenchmark measuring SDK in-memory flag evaluation duration across complex multi-rule flags
targets.input: 100,000 evaluation calls evaluated against 50 active flags with compound attribute targeting rules
targets.report: Evaluation latency benchmark summary output reporting p50, p95, and p99 percentiles

targets.method: Statistical distribution test bucketing 100,000 distinct user identifiers across a 50% rollout flag
targets.input: 100,000 synthetic UUID user identifiers hashed via MurmurHash3 against a configured 50% rollout
targets.minimum_pass: Observed percentage allocation falls between 48.5% and 51.5% (variance <= 1.5%)
targets.target: Observed percentage allocation falls between 49.2% and 50.8% (variance <= 0.8%)

targets.method: Duration from administrative dashboard kill-switch toggle until connected SSE client SDK updates local state
targets.input: Emergency kill-switch toggle dispatched across 1,000 active simulated SSE client connections
targets.minimum_pass: Connected clients update local evaluation within 150 milliseconds
targets.target: Connected clients update local evaluation within 50 milliseconds
targets.report: SSE real-time propagation timing summary log

starter_input.spec: YAML/JSON specification defining flag schema, targeting rules, rollout percentages, and sample user profiles.
starter_input.size: 50 active feature flags, 1,000 user profiles with attributes, and 100,000 evaluation request benchmark scripts
starter_input.seeded_cases: Evaluation of non-existent flags, malformed user attribute types, rapid toggle flapping, and SSE disconnection retries
starter_input.label_source: Deterministic evaluation test fixture mapping specific user IDs and attributes to expected variant outputs
starter_input.personal_data_policy: Strictly mock synthetic user IDs and fake demographic attributes; no personal data used

prerequisites: Proficiency in Go programming, HTTP web servers, and concurrent goroutines
Experience with React state management, PostgreSQL relational modeling, and Redis pub/sub

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU-bound evaluation and web UI)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source software stack via Docker Compose)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Go 1.21+, Node.js 18+, and Redis 7 installed
environment.fallback_path: In-memory mock store and polling fallback if Docker Redis pub/sub cannot be run

riskiest_component.name: SSE Connection Dropping Causing Stale Client Flag States
riskiest_component.fallback: Implement automatic client reconnection with Last-Event-ID header and periodic 30-second polling fallback

deliverables: Git repository containing Go backend API, SSE streaming service, and React admin frontend
Docker Compose file running Go server, React dashboard, PostgreSQL, and Redis
Automated load testing harness verifying MurmurHash3 distribution uniformity and p99 evaluation latency
Screener verification script executing automated benchmark and dynamic kill-switch test in under 2 minutes
out_of_scope: Machine learning multi-armed bandit automated traffic reallocation algorithms
Full-scale session recording or frontend user telemetry heatmaps
Native mobile iOS and Android SDK library packaging

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a feature flag and progressive rollout platform in Go/React with MurmurHash3 bucketing, SSE propagation, and admin audit dashboard.
worksheet.q2: Target users: platform software engineers, full-stack developers, and DevOps teams.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: progressive percentage canary rollouts, targeted subscription tier beta releases, and emergency kill-switch activation.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: deterministic MurmurHash3 bucketing, real-time SSE propagation via Redis pub/sub, sub-millisecond evaluation, and atomic audit logging.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 50 active flags, 1,000 user profiles, and 100,000 evaluation request test scripts. Synthetic profiles only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: in-memory mock store and polling.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: SSE connection dropping causing stale client states. Fallback: automatic client reconnect with Last-Event-ID header.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: hardcoded 50% split. Anti-fake check 5 creates dynamic flag with 37% rollout at runtime and asserts 37% allocation across 10,000 users.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; synthetic user profiles only.
